name: Kubernetes Cluster Security Scan (external statement)
description: Run a Trivy scan on a Kubernetes cluster, for a customer-facing assurance statement.

reporting.expectedOutput: Allowlisted assurance statement, released only for a clean assessment

notes: Sibling of sample_intent_k8s_scan_technical.json with the same target and parameters, but narrowed criteria (iso27001 only, deliberately mirroring sample_intent_image_scan_external.json). The external profile is allowlist-built with five gates: if the cluster returns any HIGH or CRITICAL finding, the external statement is withheld; if it returns none, the remaining gates (date, approval) still apply. The honest external output for an assessment that found something is nothing rather than a softened version — project_external returns {"released": false} with the unmet condition named in withheldBecause, carrying no figures, no check identifiers and no cluster name. This is also the sibling that shows a gate other than the verdict doing the work: submitting this intent against a clean cluster still yields a withheld statement, because at assessment time the job has no completion date and nobody has approved release. Both are supplied on re-projection (PUT /result/<job-id>/releaseApproval, then GET /result/<job-id>?profile=external), so a clean scan is a necessary and not a sufficient condition. With criteria ["iso27001"] alone, regulatoryCoverage.complete is true and byStatus is {assessed: 1}. Read that flag carefully: complete means every criterion the intent named was resolvable, not that ISO 27001 is covered — evidence still bears on only 3 of its 6 recorded requirements (A.8.8, A.8.27, A.8.9). The four-criteria siblings make the distinction visible by resolving to false. This family is unverified: no scan was run, so the outcome depends on the cluster.
